chunks: Sama'ah narrated from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام used to say: “Indeed, the One who counted the sand of ʿĀlij knows that the shares do not undergo ʿawl beyond six; if they were to perceive their proper aspects, they would not exceed six.”

key_terms.رَمْلَ عَالِجٍ: the sand of ʿĀlij, invoked as a sign of Allah’s vast and exact knowledge
key_terms.لَا تَعُولُ: do not undergo ʿawl, meaning they are not proportionally increased beyond their fixed legal measure
key_terms.وُجُوهَهَا: their proper aspects or legal configurations in distribution

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about the invalidity of ʿawl in inheritance law?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal principle concerning inheritance shares, affirming that the divinely ordained shares are precisely known and do not require increase beyond six through ʿawl. It attributes this ruling to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and frames it as grounded in Allah’s perfect knowledge.
